question: What are the two major branches of our immune system?
explanation: Great job! The body's defense is split into innate immunity (the fast, general guard) and adaptive immunity (the specialized, long-term force). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why does the body rely on both innate and adaptive defenses?

options.A: Innate destroys viruses while adaptive only handles bacterial infections
options.B: Innate immunity creates antibodies while adaptive creates physical barriers
options.C: Adaptive defense works entirely independently of the innate system
options.D: Innate provides immediate defense while adaptive targets specific invaders later

explanation: Spot on! Innate immunity jumps in instantly to buy time, while the adaptive system gears up to launch a precise, targeted attack. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h1)

question: Where do T-lymphocytes go to finish their maturation?
explanation: You got it! T-cells start in the bone marrow, but they travel to the thymus gland to learn how to tell friend from foe. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of secondary lymphoid organs like lymph nodes?

options.A: To destroy immature white blood cells before they enter circulation
options.B: To filter pathogens from lymph and activate adaptive immune cells
options.C: To manufacture red blood cells during severe systemic infection
options.D: To produce brand new stem cells for the circulatory system

explanation: Exactly! Lymph nodes act like security checkpoints, trapping germs so immune cells can meet them and start a fight. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which white blood cells are our most abundant and fast-acting fighters against bacteria?
explanation: Well done! Neutrophils are usually the very first white blood cells to rush to the scene of a fresh bacterial infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h3)

question: A patient has a worm infection. Which white blood cell count will likely be high on their lab results?
explanation: Correct! Eosinophils are the specialists specialized in fighting off parasites and calming down allergic reactions. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which of these is a chemical barrier part of our innate defense?

options.B: Keratin in the outer skin layer

explanation: You're right! Lysozyme is a natural germ-killer found in our tears and saliva that breaks open bacterial walls. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is healthy, unbroken skin considered part of the innate immune system?

options.A: It contains mature T-lymphocytes that destroy foreign organisms
options.B: It acts as a physical barrier that stops pathogens from entering the body
options.C: It actively manufactures specific antibodies against local skin bacteria
options.D: It produces high levels of inflammatory cytokines during minor scrapes

explanation: Spot on! Your skin is your body's first wall of defense, stopping germs from getting inside in the first place. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which cells are responsible for humoral immunity by making antibodies?
explanation: Great job! B-cells turn into plasma cells which pump out loads of antibodies into your blood and lymph. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h5)

question: A virus is hiding safely inside body cells. Which part of the immune system handles this best?

options.A: The complement protein cascade in the blood plasma
options.B: Innate physical barriers of the skin and mucous membranes

explanation: Correct! When germs hide inside cells, cytotoxic T-cells are the hit squad that hunts down and destroys those infected cells. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the final goal of the complement cascade when attacking a bacterium?

options.A: Thickening of the local epithelial basement membrane
options.B: Production of specific IgE antibodies against the bacterial wall
options.C: Maturation of naive T-cells into active helper cells
options.D: Formation of a membrane attack complex that lyses the cell

explanation: You got it! The complement system builds a 'membrane attack complex' that drills holes in the germ until it bursts (lyses). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why do blood vessels swell and open up wider during inflammation?

options.A: To prevent the complement proteins from entering the injury site
options.B: To lower local tissue temperature and stop bacterial growth
options.C: To allow white blood cells and fluid to move easily into infected tissues
options.D: To slow down local blood flow so pathogens can multiply and be counted

explanation: Spot on! Opening the blood vessels lets protective white blood cells and fluid rush straight to the injury or infection site. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main job of Regulatory T-cells (T-regs)?

options.A: To engulf large cellular debris via phagocytosis in tissues
options.B: To suppress excessive immune responses and prevent autoimmunity
options.C: To form physical barriers on mucosal and skin surfaces
options.D: To produce high affinity antibodies against foreign bacteria

explanation: Well done! T-regs act like peacekeepers, calming down the immune system after a fight so it doesn't accidentally attack healthy body tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h7)

question: What happens if the body fails to maintain proper immune tolerance?

options.A: Innate barriers permanently lose their ability to secrete mucus
options.B: Primary lymphoid organs immediately stop producing white blood cells
options.C: The immune system attacks the body's own healthy cells and tissues
options.D: The body becomes completely defenseless against minor viral colds

explanation: Correct! When tolerance fails, the body stops recognizing 'self' and starts an autoimmune attack on its own healthy organs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses give routine immunizations to patients?

options.A: To stimulate adaptive immunity and build long-term memory cells
options.B: To instantly kill any bacteria currently residing in the bloodstream
options.C: To trigger an immediate innate response via localized vasodilation
options.D: To replace missing white blood cells in immunosuppressed clients

explanation: You're doing great! Vaccines give a safe preview of a germ so your adaptive system can build memory cells for future protection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of localized inflammation checked during wound care?
explanation: Spot on! Inflammation brings extra blood, causing redness, heat, swelling, and pain—not coldness and blueness. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h8)
